chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from al-Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Only four things from perfume are forbidden to you: musk, ambergris, waras (a type of plant), and saffron; except that it is disliked for the person in ihsar (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah) to use scented oils.

key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانُ: Saffron, a spice often used in perfumes and foods
key_terms.الْعَنْبَرُ: Ambergris, a waxy substance from sperm whales used in perfumery
key_terms.الْمِسْكُ: Musk, a highly valued animal-derived scent
key_terms.الْوَرْسُ: Waras, a plant (Rhus coriaria) used for dyeing and scenting
key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: It is disliked (makruh), indicating a recommended avoidance rather than strict prohibition

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific perfumes forbidden for men in the state of Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to distinguish between specific prohibited perfumes (musk, ambergris, waras, and saffron) and the general dislike (karahah) of scented oils for the Muhrim. This clarification highlights the juristic nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the severity of prohibition versus mere recommendation in ritual consecration. The hadith serves as a practical guide for pilgrims to maintain ritual purity while avoiding unnecessary restrictions on permissible scents.
